newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower on rising interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower on rising interest rates.

text.p: Rising interest rates and the won's fall against the U.S. dollar put a dent in Seoul stocks, dragging the main index slightly lower, brokers said.
But they said hopes for a rise in the foreign stock ownership ceiling limited sharp falls.
The composite stock index shed 0.93 of a point to 657.97.

"Unstable money and foreign currency markets depressed investors' sentiment," said analyst Cha Hee-gun of Sunkyong Securities. Yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds hit a 18-month high of 12.75 percent on Tuesday and the won plunged to 883.30 against the dollar.
"Investors anticipation for raising foreign stock ownership ceiling limited sharp falls," Cha said.
The anticipation bouyed core blue chips, foreign investors' favourites. Samsung Electronics rose 1,000 won to 56,000 and POSCO added 100 won to 43,100.
But Tongyang Securities's Woo Sang-chul said: "I question how much foreign funds will really flow to the bourse. Right now, investors are like drowning men clutching at straws."
The Finance and Economy Minister Kang Kyong-shik is due to unveil a new economic package on Thursday, which investors believe will be aimed at boosting the sagging economy.
Among anticipated measures are the expansion of the foreign stock ownership ceiling, and measures to lower high interest rate and to help soothe tight liquidity.
Investors were hoping the government would come up with a revision of the real name financial system to lure black market money into the economy and the stock market.

But the anticipation fizzled out as President Kim Young-sam urged the finance minister late Monday to leave the basic principle behind the system alone, which is one of Kim's salvoes in a war against corruption and tax evasion.

After the market closed, minister Kang told reporters the government would push legislation banning money laundering to prevent corruption and accumulation of slush funds. He also said his ministry would exempt small companies from probes into funding sources.
"I don't expect much from Thursday's annoucement," Samsung Securities analyst said.
"It will contain nothing substantial as there is no quick remedy to cure the structural problem of our economy," he added.
Buying remained strong in selective small-capitalised shares with good company earnings prospects.
Both Sewon and Dae Young Package went limit up, gaining 6,600 won and 3,400 won to 90,000 and 46,600 respectively.
Brokers said the main index would hover around the 650 level until Thursday and said they expected no sharp fluctuations for the time being.
But the Samsung Securities analyst said: "I cannot rule out the possibility the market will nosedive if there is no sign of a turn around in economic fundamentals."
